notableFacts.text: Polaris is the North Star, close to the direction of Earth's northern celestial pole.
Aldebaran is one of the stars outlining the Winter Circle.
Capella is one of the stars outlining the Winter Circle.
Rigel is one of the stars outlining the Winter Circle.
Betelgeuse is one corner of the Winter Triangle.
Sirius is the brightest star in Earth's night sky.
Sirius is one corner of the Winter Triangle.
Procyon is one corner of the Winter Triangle.
Pollux is one of the stars outlining the Winter Circle.
Merak is one of the Big Dipper's two pointer stars used to find Polaris.
Dubhe and Merak are the Big Dipper's pointer stars toward Polaris.
Phecda is one of the four stars outlining the Big Dipper's bowl.
Megrez links the Big Dipper's bowl and handle.
Alioth lies in the Big Dipper's handle.
Mizar is a star in the Big Dipper's handle, seen near Alcor.
Mizar is a star in the Big Dipper's handle, seen near Alcor.
Spica is one corner of the Diamond of Virgo asterism.
Alkaid marks the tip of the Big Dipper's handle.
Arcturus is one corner of the Diamond of Virgo asterism.
Vega forms one corner of the Summer Triangle with Deneb and Altair.
Vega was once Earth's northern pole star due to axial precession.
Altair forms one corner of the Summer Triangle.
Altair rotates so rapidly that its shape is flattened.
Deneb forms one corner of the Summer Triangle.
